To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a new class of SAW devices, the unapodized periodic IDTs, is introduced, (ii) the surface charge distribution on the electrodes of an unapodized SAW transducer is determined by solving a system of algebraic equations, (iii) the system is solved by a Galerkin method and by a collocation method, and (iv) both the Galerkin and the collocation method yield algebraic equations having Toeplitz structures.

the surface charge on an unapodized periodic IDT with J electrodes can be determined by solving a linear system with one or two-dimensional Toeplitzc structure, and that the solution can be obtained with high accuracy by the Galerkin and the collocation methods.

(i) a new class of SAW transducers, the so-called periodic IDTs, can be designed and optimized by the use of the new theory and the associated numerical methods, and (ii) the theory and the numerical methods can be used in the design and optimization of SAW devices that have a large number of elements, such as the SAW convolvers and correlators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of numerical methods for the solution of integral equations governing the surface charge distribution on an array of electrodes on a piezoelectric crystal.
the determination of surface charge on periodic SAW transducers.

a class of integral equations that are of interest in a number of areas, including the analysis of periodic arrays of electrodes on SAW transducers and the analysis of the interaction of acoustic waves and periodic arrays of objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of an unapodized transducer with a periodic electrode structure is not a good choice for the design of a SAW filter.
the use of the collocation method is not recommended for the calculation of the surface charge distribution on a SAW transducer.
the surface charge on an unapodized SAW transducer is a function of the transducer geometry and the electrical properties of the substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the integral equation approach is a viable alternative to finite element techniques for the analysis of periodic structures.
the Galerkin method is more efficient and the collocation method is more accurate.
the Galerkin and collocation methods are equivalent and that they both yield exact solutions to the integral equation for an infinite number of electrodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface charge distribution on a periodic array is a superposition of a set of charge distributions, each of which is a solution of a simpler integral equation.
the Galerkin solution is a good approximation to the collocation solution.

, for periodic SAW devices, the surface charge distribution can be accurately determined using the Galerkin method with a single basis function, and the charge distribution can be efficiently computed using the collocation method with a small number of basis functions.
